builds.name: Raised bed (untreated lumber, 10 in tall)
builds.good_for: Gardeners with a yard or patio who want clean, loose soil, fewer weeds, earlier spring warming, and a barrier against unknown or lead-contaminated ground soil.
steps: Pick a level spot with the most sun.
Cut boards to length (most stores will cut them for free).
Screw the corners together with 3 in exterior screws, 3 per corner.
Lay cardboard on the ground inside the frame to smother grass.
Fill with raised-bed soil mix and water it in.

builds.name: Container garden setup
builds.good_for: Balconies, patios, steps, renters, and windowsills. No digging, movable to follow the sun, and avoids ground soil completely.
steps: Choose pots with drainage holes (fabric grow bags are cheap and light).
Fill with fresh potting mix, never garden soil.
Group pots where they get the most sun; use saucers indoors.
Water when the top inch is dry; containers dry out faster than beds.

builds.name: Cattle-panel trellis
builds.good_for: Climbing or vining crops (pole beans, peas, cucumbers, tomatoes) in a small footprint; saves space by growing up instead of out.
steps: Drive T-posts on the north edge of the bed so the trellis does not shade other plants.
Stand the cattle panel against the posts and zip-tie it at three heights.
Plant climbers along the base and guide the first tendrils onto the panel.

builds.name: Cold frame (3 × 6 ft)
builds.good_for: Extending the season: hardy greens through late fall and early spring, hardening off seedlings, and starting a garden in the off-season.
steps: Build a bottomless box from 2×10 boards, back side one board taller than the front so rain runs off.
Screw two hinges to the back and attach the clear twin-wall lid.
Face the slope south. Prop the lid open on sunny days above 50 °F so plants do not cook.

screws.item: 3 in exterior deck screws (1 lb box)

builds.name: Rain barrel
builds.good_for: Anyone with a downspout. Collects free water for summer dry spells; most useful for larger gardens or where a hose is far away.
steps: Set two layers of cinder blocks next to a downspout so the spigot is high enough for a watering can.
Cut the downspout and install the diverter kit.
Use the water for soil and roots, not on leafy greens you eat raw (roof runoff is not potable).

builds.name: Wire compost bin
builds.good_for: Turning leaves, grass clippings and kitchen scraps into free soil amendment; great fall project since leaves are plentiful.
steps: Unroll about 10 ft of welded wire and form a 3 ft wide circle.
Zip-tie the ends together and set it on bare ground in partial shade.
Layer browns (leaves) and greens (kitchen scraps) roughly 3:1; keep it as damp as a wrung-out sponge.

wire.item: Welded wire fencing, 36 in × 25 ft roll

builds.name: Drip irrigation with hose timer
builds.good_for: Larger gardens, frequent travelers, and anyone who forgets to water. Saves water and keeps leaves dry, which reduces disease.
steps: Connect the timer, backflow preventer and pressure regulator at the spigot.
Run 1/2 in mainline to the bed and lay emitter lines about 12 in apart.
Run it for 20 minutes and check that the soil is moist 4 in down; adjust the timer.

kit.item: Raised-bed drip irrigation kit (covers ~50 sq ft)

builds.name: Low tunnel (mini hoop house)
builds.good_for: Season extension over a whole bed: earlier spring plantings, later fall harvests, and protecting crops from frost and pests.
steps: Bend 10 ft lengths of 1/2 in PVC into hoops every 3–4 ft along the bed.
Slip each end over a rebar stake driven 12 in into the ground.
Drape greenhouse film or frost cloth over the hoops and clip it; weigh down the edges.
Vent the ends on sunny days.
